correctness.rationale: For the substitution-fixed Tribonacci word, cited Richomme–Saari–Zamboni 2-balance theorem bounds every same-length factor Parikh difference d by |di|<=2 with sum di=0. An independent integer enumeration found exactly 18 nonzero such vectors: permutations/signs of (1,−1,0),(2,−2,0),(2,−1,−1). A nonzero weight-kernel direction therefore requires equality of two weights or 2ai=aj+ak. Converse: if two weights equal, distinct singletons collide; if midpoint, three concrete factor-pair witnesses 020/101, 01001/20102, 102010102/001020100 have independent verified Parikh differences (1,−2,1),(1,1,−2),(−2,1,1) and occur in an independently generated Tribonacci fixed-point prefix. Hence all six hyperplanes necessary/sufficient for equality of additive and abelian complexity for EVERY length; finite witness search supplements, not replaces published infinite 2-balance theorem.
